NATP00075.par1.translation: Quantity of matter is measured jointly by density and volume.

NATP00075.par3.translation: Quantity of motion is measured jointly by velocity and quantity of matter.

NATP00075.par5.translation: Inherent force resists alteration of rest or uniform rectilinear motion.

NATP00075.par7.translation: Impressed force is an action changing rest or uniform rectilinear motion.

NATP00075.par9.translation: Centripetal force draws, impels or directs a body toward a point as centre.

NATP00075.par13.translation: Accelerative force is measured in proportion to velocity generated in a given time.

NATP00075.par15.translation: Motive force is measured in proportion to motion generated in a given time.

NATP00075.par18.translation: Motive force is accelerative force multiplied by quantity of matter.

NATP00076.par1.translation: A body persists in rest or uniform rectilinear motion except as impressed forces change that state.

NATP00076.par3.translation: Change of motion is proportional to impressed motive force and directed along its line.

NATP00076.par4.translation: Doubling or tripling the force doubles or triples generated motion; existing motion is composed with it.

NATP00076.par7.translation: A body under combined forces describes the diagonal in the time in which it would describe the sides separately.

NATP00076.par8.translation: Construct the parallelogram; each force leaves the approach to the parallel opposite side unchanged, so the body reaches their intersection.

NATP00077.par25.translation: With a fixed angle of intersection and ordinate angle, the vanishing areas have the duplicate ratio of corresponding sides. The statement says triangles; the proof treats curvilinear areas.

NATP00077.par26.translation: Extend and rescale the ordinates; the tangent and limiting secant coincide, and similar areas have the duplicate side ratio.

NATP00077.par27.translation: Spaces described at the beginning of motion have the duplicate ratio of times. The force wording is edition-specific.

NATP00077.par28.translation: Represent times by abscissae and generated velocities by ordinates: spaces correspond to the swept areas, invoking Lemma IX.

NATP00082.par32.translation: Initially described spaces vary jointly as forces and squares of times.

NATP00082.par33.translation: Hence forces vary directly as initially described spaces and inversely as squares of times.

NATP00082.par34.translation: Squares of times vary directly as described spaces and inversely as forces.

NATP00077.par45.translation: Divide time equally. Inertia gives equal successive unforced segments; parallel central impulse preserves triangle area. Increase triangle number and decrease width; Lemma III corollary 4 is cited for a curved limiting perimeter. Newton then asserts uninterrupted central action.

NATP00077.par6.translation: Take AF equal to the greatest width. Its rectangle exceeds the difference of enclosing figures and becomes smaller than any given rectangle as that width diminishes.

Increase triangle number and decrease width; Lemma III corollary 4 is cited for a curved limiting perimeter. Newton then asserts uninterrupted central action.

NATP00082.par7.translation: Take AF equal to the greatest width. Its rectangle exceeds the difference of enclosing figures and becomes smaller than any given rectangle as that width diminishes.

NATP00089.par9.translation: Equal time cells and central impulses yield equal triangles; infinitely many infinitely small triangles are asserted to give uninterrupted force. No numbered limiting lemma is cited in this passage.

NATP00090.par17.translation: Equal time cells and central impulses yield equal triangles; infinitely many infinitely small triangles are asserted to give uninterrupted force. No numbered limiting lemma is cited in this passage.

NATP00077.par32.translation: For normal contact subtense BD, circle geometry gives AB squared = AG times BD. The limiting intercept AI is approached as the points coalesce.

NATP00077.par39.translation: The contact angle is neither infinitely smaller nor infinitely greater than circular contact: the intercept AI is finite. Powers above or below the quadratic order are counterexamples to omitting this restriction.

NATP00077.par37.translation: By the nature of the parabola, the curvilinear area is two thirds of the triangle and the segment one third; these areas are therefore cubic in tangent, chord or arc.

NATP00082.par37.translation: For normal contact subtense BD, circle geometry gives AB squared = AG times BD. The limiting intercept AI is approached as the points coalesce.

NATP00082.par45.translation: The contact angle is neither infinitely smaller nor infinitely greater than circular contact: the intercept AI is finite. Powers above or below the quadratic order are counterexamples to omitting this restriction.

NATP00082.par44.translation: By the nature of the parabola, the curvilinear area is two thirds of the triangle and the segment one third; these areas are therefore cubic in tangent, chord or arc.

NATP00082.par89.translation: At fixed time sagitta varies with force by proposition I corollary 4; its quadratic time scaling invokes lemma XI corollaries 2 and 3.

NATP00082.par90.translation: The same is also easily demonstrated by corollary 4 of lemma X.

NATP00082.par91.translation: QR equals the sagitta of the doubled arc whose midpoint is P; the doubled triangle supplies the corresponding time measure.

NATP00082.par93.translation: The force ratio uses the curvature-circle chord through the force centre and the squared perpendicular from centre to tangent. The 1726 wording additionally admits concentric crossing.

NATP00087.par88.translation: The same is also easily demonstrated by corollary 4 of lemma X.

NATP00077.par77.translation: Generated QR at fixed time follows force by law II; at fixed force follows squared time by lemma X. Sector area supplies elapsed time.

NATP00089.par10.translation: Bodies moving uniformly on circles have centripetal forces jointly as the squares of simultaneously described arcs and inversely as the radii.

NATP00089.par11.translation: The proof compares tangent departures for vanishing arcs and substitutes the circle radii for the limiting geometric denominators; it cites no numbered lemma.

NATP00090.par18.translation: Bodies moving uniformly on circles have centripetal forces jointly as the squares of simultaneously described arcs and inversely as the radii.

NATP00090.par19.translation: The proof compares tangent departures for vanishing arcs and substitutes the circle radii for the limiting geometric denominators; it cites no numbered lemma.

NATP00076.par20.translation: Motions relative to one another are unchanged when the enclosing space is at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line.

NATP00076.par22.translation: Equal accelerative forces applied along parallel lines to all bodies leave their relative motions unchanged.

NATP00076.par23.translation: Law II is given as the reason: equal parallel accelerations do not change relative positions and motions.

NATP00081.par20.translation: Motions relative to one another are unchanged when the enclosing space is at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line.

NATP00081.par22.translation: Equal accelerative forces applied along parallel lines to all bodies leave their relative motions unchanged.

NATP00081.par23.translation: Law II is given as the reason: equal parallel accelerations do not change relative positions and motions.

NATP00077.par14.translation: Corresponding sides of similar figures are proportional, and their areas are in the duplicate ratio of the sides.

NATP00077.par17.translation: A vanishing arc, its chord and its tangent have the ultimate ratio of equality.

NATP00077.par48.translation: A body describing a curved line and areas proportional to times about a fixed or uniformly translating point is urged by a centripetal force toward that point.

NATP00077.par49.translation: Case 1 infers the direction of the deflecting force from Law I, Euclid I.40 and Law II for an immobile point.

NATP00077.par50.translation: Case 2 invokes corollary 5 of the laws to transfer the result to a point and figure moving uniformly in a straight line.

NATP00077.par53.translation: For areas about another moving body, the first body's force is composed from a centripetal force toward the second body and the second body's whole accelerative force.

NATP00077.par54.translation: Using corollary 6 of the laws, add equal contrary parallel acceleration to both bodies; Law I fixes the reference body's resulting motion and Proposition II identifies the remaining force as central.

NATP00077.par60.translation: For uniform motions on different circles, centripetal forces tend to the circle centres and are jointly as squared simultaneously described arcs and inversely as radii.

NATP00077.par61.translation: The proof cites Proposition II for direction and Lemmas V and XI for the limiting tangent-departure ratio.

NATP00082.par18.translation: A vanishing arc, its chord and its tangent have the ultimate ratio of equality.

NATP00082.par58.translation: A body describing a plane curve and areas proportional to times about a fixed or uniformly translating point is urged by a centripetal force toward that point.

NATP00082.par59.translation: Case 1 infers the direction of the deflecting force from Law I, Euclid I.40 and Law II for an immobile point.

NATP00082.par60.translation: Case 2 invokes corollary 5 of the laws to transfer the result to a point and figure moving uniformly in a straight line.

NATP00082.par71.translation: For uniform motions on different circles, centripetal forces tend to the circle centres and are jointly as squared simultaneously described arcs and inversely as radii.

NATP00082.par72.translation: The proof explicitly cites Proposition II, Proposition I corollaries 2 and 4, and Lemma VII.

NATP00077.par40.translation: Section I Scholium: the lemmas replace the method of indivisibles by ultimate sums and ratios; where quantities are later treated as made of particles, or small curves as straight, evanescent divisible quantities and limits of sums and ratios are meant.

NATP00082.par46.translation: Section I Scholium: the lemmas replace the method of indivisibles by ultimate sums and ratios; where quantities are later treated as made of particles, or small curves as straight, evanescent divisible quantities and limits of sums and ratios are meant.

NATP00077.par42.translation: Objection: ultimate ratios would imply ultimate magnitudes and indivisibles. Reply: ultimate ratios are limits which the ratios of quantities decreasing without limit approach closer than any given difference, never exceed, and do not attain before the quantities are diminished in infinitum.

NATP00082.par48.translation: Objection: ultimate ratios would imply ultimate magnitudes and indivisibles. Reply: ultimate ratios are limits which the ratios of quantities decreasing without limit approach closer than any given difference, never exceed, and do not attain before the quantities are diminished in infinitum.

NATP00077.par84.translation: Proposition IX statement: a body revolves in a spiral cutting all radii at a given angle; the law of centripetal force toward the centre of the spiral is required.

NATP00082.par108.translation: Proposition IX statement: a body revolves in a spiral cutting all radii at a given angle; the law of centripetal force toward the centre of the spiral is required.

NATP00077.par85.translation: Proposition IX solution (1687): by Lemma XI the ratio QT^2/QR is as SP, so QT^2*SP^2/QR is as SP^3; the conclusion is printed as "vis centripeta ut cubus distantiae SP", citing the corollary of Theorem V.

NATP00082.par109.translation: Proposition IX solution (1713): the same ratio argument; the conclusion reads "vis centripeta est reciproce ut cubus distantiae SP", citing Proposition VI corollaries 1 and 5.

NATP00077.par305.translation: Proposition XLI corollary 3: under a centripetal force inversely as the cube of the distance, a body leaving V perpendicular to CV with the proper speed follows the constructed trajectory; in the hyperbola case it descends to the centre, in the ellipse case it ascends forever and goes off to infinity.

NATP00082.par335.translation: Proposition XLI corollary 3: under a centripetal force inversely as the cube of the distance, a body leaving V perpendicular to CV with the proper speed follows the constructed trajectory; in the hyperbola case it descends to the centre, in the ellipse case it ascends forever and goes off to infinity.

NATP00077.par325.translation: Proposition XLV corollary 1: a power-law force can be found from the motion of the apsides. A force decreasing faster than the cube of the altitude: a body leaving an apsis descends to the centre or ascends to infinity. A force decreasing more slowly, or increasing: the body never descends to the centre and reaches a lower apsis.

NATP00082.par355.translation: Proposition XLV corollary 1: a power-law force can be found from the motion of the apsides. A force decreasing faster than the cube of the altitude (1713 adds "in recessu a centro"): a body leaving an apsis descends to the centre or ascends to infinity. A force decreasing more slowly, or increasing: the body never descends to the centre and reaches a lower apsis.
